_about: M06's own last-resort questions, used ONLY when M05 cannot be reached (spec §10).
Stems, concepts and key points are copied from M05's authored playlist
the same thing M05 would; follow-ups and hints are added because the ladder needs them.
These turns are NOT sent to M13: M13 resolves a question package from M05, and these
ids do not exist there. The report says so. Keep this list short on purpose - if it is

items.label: fb_complexity_of_a_loop
items.stem: You have a single loop over an array of n elements doing constant work each pass. What is the time complexity, and why?

key_points.statement: States the complexity is linear in n.
Justifies it by constant work repeated n times.

follow_ups.template: What would change if the loop body called a function that itself looped over the array?
Why do we drop constants when we write that down?
Can you think of a case where the constant actually matters in practice?

hint_ladder: Think about how many times the body runs.
If each pass costs the same, what does the total grow with?

items.label: fb_stack_vs_queue
items.stem: Give me a problem that needs a stack and one that needs a queue.

key_points.statement: Gives a last-in-first-out use for the stack.
Gives a first-in-first-out use for the queue.

follow_ups.template: Why does your stack example need last-in-first-out specifically?
How would you build a queue if all you had were two stacks?
What does each operation cost in that two-stack queue, on average?

hint_ladder: Think about something that has to be undone in reverse order.
Think about something that has to be served in the order it arrived.

items.label: fb_dictionary_use_case
items.stem: You need to count how many times each word appears in a document. What structure do you use and why?

key_points.statement: Chooses a hash map or dictionary.
Justifies it by constant-time lookup on arbitrary keys.

follow_ups.template: Why is lookup in that structure fast?
What makes it constant time, rather than something slower?
And if two different words hash to the same slot?
When would you pick a sorted structure over it instead?

hint_ladder: You want to go from a word straight to its count.
Which structure maps an arbitrary key to a value in one step?

items.label: fb_recursion_in_your_own_words
items.stem: Explain recursion to someone who has just learned loops.

key_points.statement: Describes a function calling itself on a smaller input.
Mentions a stopping condition or base case.

follow_ups.template: What happens if the base case is missing?
Where does the computer keep track of the calls that haven't finished yet?
When would you rewrite a recursive solution as a loop, and why?

hint_ladder: Think about solving a smaller version of the same problem.
What stops it from going on forever?
